messages.author: 8aa9b8cc06fdc99c
messages.subject: binomial distribution test failure
parts:
I don't know how much this matters, but we're now
off in the fourth significant digit, which seems like
a mile:

src/test/prob/distributions/univariate/discrete/binomial_test.cpp:5: Failure
Value of: stan::prob::binomial_log(10,20,0.4)
Actual: -2.140208
Expected: -2.144372
[ FAILED ] ProbDistributionsBinomial.Binomial (0 ms)

The test that fails is:

EXPECT_FLOAT_EQ(-2.144372, stan::prob::binomial_log(10,20,0.4));

I used R to generate the value to test against:

> dbinom(10,20,0.4,log=T)
[1] -2.144372

I just reduced the arithmetic precision on that particular
test to 0.005 and it passes, but just wanted to bring this up in case
it's an issue.

- Bob

approximation is much more appropriate for arguments > 1000 than
arguments > 10. Sorry about that.
